reason: The cited evidence shows containerless laser melting with levitation (E1) and CALPHAD modeling for oxides (E2), but neither demonstrates high-speed DSC on HEAs, extraction of thermodynamic properties from DSC via CALPHAD, nor the claimed accuracy; key premises thus lack direct support.
premises: Containerless laser melting prevents contamination and yields intrinsic thermal signals
High-speed DSC can capture precise melting events under fast heating rates
CALPHAD modeling can extract melting temperature, enthalpy, entropy, and volume change from DSC signatures
Established CALPHAD databases (e.g., Zinkevich) are applicable to HEAs
The combined approach achieves quantitative accuracy (e.g., ±5–10°C, ±5–10%)
